# SciNTech

SciNTech uses science to make useful Android tools that work offline. Its apps do their core work on the phone, without a connection, and their core features are free. Current apps: Watermark Remover, which learns a repeating, tiled watermark from two or more photos carrying the same mark and lifts it off, Seamless Video Looper, which finds a loop point in a video and renders a forward-playing seamless loop, and Pic2Ink, which prepares a photo for an NFC e-ink frame and sends it from the phone (closed test, not yet on Google Play). Photos and videos are not uploaded to be processed.

All apps on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/developer?id=SciNTech (Pic2Ink is not listed there until it leaves its closed test). Machine-readable list of the apps: https://scintech-dev.github.io/apps.json

Support: each app's Settings → Send feedback. Privacy and data-deletion requests: the contact or data-removal section of each app's privacy policy.

## Values

Real technique, not decoration: each app aims established methods at one practical problem and names them.
Offline, and free at the core: each app's core work runs on the phone without a connection, and its core features are free.
Awareness through measurement: each app measures the hardware it works with and the result it produces: it sets its defaults from the first and shows you the second.
Honest about what won't work: each app states the cases it handles badly.
Predictable, and yours to adjust: every report an app sends is a switch in Settings.

## Watermark Remover

Status: on Google Play for everyone since 2026-10-15, listed as "Watermark Remover (Offline)": https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.watermarkremover.android (package com.watermarkremover.android). Current release 0.5.0 (build 68); the first production release was 0.2.13.

Pages:
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/watermark-remover/ — What the app does and does not do, in four steps.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/watermark-remover/how-it-works/ — The four ideas: find the repeat, learn the mark from many copies, lift it off, fill what was lost; plus the neural one-photo path (on the device, with a mirrored-pass self-check).
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/watermark-remover/examples/ — Main case: a watermark file opened in the app and removed from two pictures; also a mark learned from 8 photos and saved, and two photos; synthetic, scored against the true clean image over the whole frame, one page with filters; plus a "One photo" section (0.6.0) with 7 before/after pairs on public-domain photographs.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/watermark-remover/compatibility/ — Requirements, inputs and outputs, and answers to common questions.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/watermark-remover/privacy/ — Privacy at a glance, and the full policy at #policy.

Facts:

- Requires Android 8.0 (API 26) or later.
- Photos are processed on the device; no photo or result is uploaded. A feedback report may include a screenshot only if the user attaches one.
- Works offline: learning and removing the mark run on the phone and need no connection.
- The app contains no advertising or analytics SDK. Reports use an anonymous Firebase identifier.
- Easy mode (0.5.0): one Add button for pictures, clean originals and watermark files; the app sorts them and asks only when unsure, and Skip is always safe. From 0.7.2 a single photo goes straight to the on-device one-photo model and shows the result, with Not perfect to touch it up by hand; Skip and Not a pair keep both pictures in the job as watermarked photos, and the pair is not suggested again. Bursts of one scene count once. Pictures of different sizes can be cleaned together when the watermark repeats.
- Learns the watermark from two or more of your photos that carry the same mark, and can save it to remove it from new photos later; 5–8 learning photos are recommended. From 0.6.0 (rolling out 2026-10) a neural model on the device also removes a mark from one photo, and is used for 2 photos when the learner cannot find a shared mark; it needs about 1.2 GB free memory and the full (non-Lite) build. Measured on the developers' test set: median +6.5 dB whole-picture improvement, 0 of 100 clean photos altered, visibly damaged patches on 2 of 300 marked pictures; about 20 s per 12 MP photo on a 2025 flagship, about 100 s on a 2020 mid-range phone. Results vary; the app shows a "Mark remaining" estimate relative to the input, and a Not perfect button opens a template editor to refine the learned mark.
- Synthetic tests (examples pages): a mark learned from 8 photos and saved, applied to two new pictures, 21 kinds of mark: 41 of 42 results closer to the true picture, 1 further, 0 declined, mean +11.12 dB. Learned from the two pictures themselves: 36 closer, 0 further, 6 declined, mean +6.93 dB (+5.15 dB on repeating marks, +8.54 dB on single marks).
- Removes repeating or tiled semi-transparent watermarks. Before 0.6.0 a single standalone logo could not be removed from one photo alone (nothing to compare); the 0.6.0 one-photo model can, with some modest results; learned from 8 photos and saved, 10 of 11 single-mark kinds ended closer on both new pictures in synthetic tests; the 11th was closer on one and further on the other.
- Where a mark hid the picture completely, the filled area is a reconstruction, not the original: the MI-GAN model on the device in the standard build, a classical fill in the lite build.
- A Hardware Test picks the removal engine; it is the first item in the ⋮ menu on every screen. Its results are shared by default since 0.2.3 and can be switched off in Settings.
- A self-test on built-in sample photos (no user photos) runs once per install and again after some app or system updates, not daily; sharing its results has its own switch in Settings.
- Opening the app makes no network connection of its own; the app signs in anonymously to Firebase only when a report is about to be sent.
- Crash and out-of-memory reports are on by default and can be switched off in Settings.
- Feedback is sent from the corner button or Send feedback in the ⋮ menu on any screen, with an optional screenshot; it is the only support channel.
- The core features are free.
- Input: images chosen in the Android picker or shared to the app. Output: saved as JPEG or PNG, or shared as PNG. No photo-library permission is requested.
- Whether a particular photo may be altered is a question of the photographer's or owner's rights; use the app on photos you have the right to restore.

## Seamless Video Looper

Status: on Google Play, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.seamlessvideolooper.android — current release 1.7.5. App pages are at /seamless-video-looper/.

- Requires Android 8.0 (API 26) or later.
- Finds candidate loop points, previews them, and renders a loop that always plays forward (not a boomerang).
- Loop search, stabilization, blending, audio processing and rendering run on the device; video files are not uploaded.
- Output is an MP4 with H.264/AVC video and, when audio is kept, AAC-LC audio. Renders carry no app watermark.
- A Hardware Test checks memory, decoding and the optional motion methods and sets defaults from the result.
- Built on named techniques: NeuFlow v2 optical flow, RIFE frame interpolation, OpenCV ORB feature matching.
- Fast foreground crossings, occlusion and large camera moves can leave a visible seam.
- Core features are free and work offline; the current release is free. The app contains no advertising or general usage-analytics SDK.

## Pic2Ink

Status: closed test, not yet on Google Play (package com.scintech.pic2ink, version 0.1.0). Based on DITHR by redphx (MIT licence).

Pages:
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/pic2ink/ — What the app does in three steps, what it handles and does not.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/pic2ink/how-it-works/ — Dithering to a panel's few inks, the exact buffer, the NFC send, measuring the bezel from a photo.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/pic2ink/compatibility/ — Requirements, the frames table generated from the app's catalogue (tested / not tested), FAQ.
- https://scintech-dev.github.io/pic2ink/privacy/ — Privacy at a glance, and the full policy at #policy.

Facts:

- Requires Android 7.0 (API 24) or later. NFC is needed for NFC frames, not for devices that take a picture file (PNG export).
- Three steps: choose the device (brand and model), choose the picture (photo picker or Share; crop by dragging, rotate 90°), send via NFC.
- Catalogue (from DITHR, generated from the app's own list at einksend 6fb6fe2): 31 NFC entries (27 profiles and 4 variants) and 21 file-export devices. Tested with Pic2Ink: TapMora Spectra 6 photo frame only (2026-10-28); every other entry is "in catalogue, not tested with Pic2Ink".
- The picture is prepared at the panel's exact resolution (TapMora 304×400) in the panel's inks only, using DITHR's error diffusion: Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson, Jarvis, Ostromoukhov or none; the default is DITHR's Atkinson/Jarvis hybrid.
- A send is reported as "confirmed" (the frame reported its refresh finished) or "sent, not confirmed"; nothing is retried automatically.
- Measure bezel: sends an edge ruler, reads from one photo of the frame how many pixels each edge hides (about ±1 px), and saves the values for that frame after the user checks them.
- Auto-detect (experimental): a read-only scan identifies an unknown frame's protocol family from its reply.
- Free; no account. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any frame maker.
- Pictures are prepared on the phone and sent only to the frame the user taps, over NFC.
- Pictures are never uploaded. Automatic crash, failure and self-test reports (error types, code locations, phone facts; never a picture, file name, Wi-Fi name or frame identifier) are on by default, each kind with a switch in Settings; feedback is sent only when the user presses Send. There are no accounts, no advertising and no analytics software.
- A feedback report's screenshot is ticked by default and can show the user's picture if it is on screen; it can be unticked before sending.
- Reports carry three anonymous identifiers (a random install identifier, Android ID, and a Firebase anonymous sign-in identifier), used only to group reports from one phone.
- Sent reports are deleted within 30 days of a request; the policy's "Removing your data" section says how to ask.
